findings.title: Spectrum ID mismatch returns wrong error code vs contract
findings.message: The export.start contract added in this diff says a wrong spectrum ID returns `not-found` ("spectrum ID is not the exact current result"). The implementation returns `not-ready` instead. Clients that branch on the documented error code will mishandle this failure.
findings.suggestion: Make the code and the contract agree. Return `not-found` for an ID mismatch, and keep `not-ready` only for the case where no completed spectrum exists. Alternatively, update the contract to match the code.
findings.evidence: return &actionError{"not-ready", "Choose the exact result ID of the current completed spectrum"}

fix.before: return &actionError{"not-ready", "Choose the exact result ID of the current completed spectrum"}
fix.after: return &actionError{"not-found", "Choose the exact result ID of the current completed spectrum"}

findings.title: Absent params cause unmarshal error
findings.message: The contract says empty analyze params should reuse the current settings. If the caller omits params, the `RawMessage` is zero-length, and `json.Unmarshal` fails with "unexpected end of JSON input" instead of falling back to the current settings.
findings.suggestion: Treat empty or whitespace-only raw as no fields before calling `Unmarshal`.

findings.title: Unit-text fundamental is not decoded via SpectrumInput
findings.message: The capability schema says `fundamental_hz` accepts decimal text with units ("Hz/kHz/mHz"). The comment says `SpectrumInput` exists to accept that unit text. However, the command decodes params straight into `SpectrumParams`, whose `Fundamental` field is a plain `float64`. If the custom unmarshalling lives on `SpectrumInput`, string inputs like "1 kHz" are rejected even though the schema advertises them.
findings.suggestion: Decode into `SpectrumInput`, which carries the unit-aware unmarshalling, then convert: `var in SpectrumInput; if err := params(raw, &in); err != nil {...}; p = SpectrumParams(in)`.

		if err := params(raw, &p); err != nil {

findings.title: Spectrum canvas revision ignores appearance changes
findings.message: The spectrum mesh uses theme palette colors (`palette.Grid`, `palette.Accent`, `palette.Muted`), but its redraw revision only tracks `state.CommandRevision`. The scope and sweep canvases track appearance through `canvasAppearanceRevision`. When the theme is "system" and the OS appearance changes, or reduce-motion changes, the command revision stays the same. The cached spectrum mesh can then keep stale colors.
findings.suggestion: Add a `spectrumAppearance canvasAppearanceRevision` to `screen`. Combine it with `CommandRevision` when setting `spectrumDrawing.Revision`, the same way the scope and sweep canvases do.

findings.title: Unchecked type assertion on schema properties
findings.message: `SchemaRegistry` writes into the result of `timeInputSchema` with an unchecked type assertion on `schema["properties"]`. If `timeInputSchema` returns a schema whose properties are missing or of another type, the assertion panics and takes down the registry or catalog. If the `fundamental_hz` key does not exist, the write silently adds an undeclared property. This depends on the shape `timeInputSchema` returns, which is not shown in this part.
findings.suggestion: Use the comma-ok form, and fail loudly in tests if the property is missing. For example: `props, ok := schema["properties"].(map[string]any); if !ok { panic("spectrum schema missing properties") }`. Alternatively, check that `fundamental_hz` exists before overriding it.

findings.title: export.start id description omits spectrum kinds
findings.message: spectrum-json/csv were added to the kind enum, but the `id` field description was not updated. It does not say that spectrum kinds require the exact current spectrum result ID. The `x-work-inventory`/effects text likewise only mentions verification/sweep capture semantics.
findings.suggestion: Update the id description to mention that spectrum kinds require the exact current spectrum result ID.
findings.evidence: inputProperty(schema, "id")["description"] = "Omitted/null/empty means no recording ID. Audio-WAV requires the exact current completed preview ID; verification/sweep kinds look up this value and return not-found when absent/unknown; schematic/scope kinds reject a nonempty ID."

fix.before: inputProperty(schema, "id")["description"] = "Omitted/null/empty means no recording ID. Audio-WAV requires the exact current completed preview ID; verification/sweep kinds look up this value and return not-found when absent/unknown; schematic/scope kinds reject a nonempty ID."
fix.after: inputProperty(schema, "id")["description"] = "Omitted/null/empty means no recording ID. Audio-WAV requires the exact current completed preview ID; spectrum kinds require the exact current spectrum result ID; verification/sweep kinds look up this value and return not-found when absent/unknown; schematic/scope kinds reject a nonempty ID."

findings.title: Spectrum artifact lacks electrical revision provenance
findings.message: The contract says retained work exposes captured generation/run/electrical or record identity. Other kinds populate ElectricalRevision from the captured data, but the spectrum branch does not. This leaves the artifact provenance incomplete.
findings.suggestion: Populate capture.artifact.ElectricalRevision (and RunID, if known) from the spectrum result's source metadata.

findings.title: Minimum-row check uses un-deduplicated rows
findings.message: The minimum-sample check counts raw rows before duplicate timestamps are collapsed. The contract promises at least 32 distinct sample intervals, but a recording with many duplicate timestamps passes this check. Because `n` is at least 32 and `dt` must be at least `maxGap`, such a recording then fails later with a confusing grid error.
findings.suggestion: After deduplication, also require `len(rows) >= 33`, i.e. 32 distinct intervals, and return the same clear message when it fails.

findings.title: JSON export returns data alongside error
findings.message: When marshalling fails, the function still returns a non-nil one-byte payload alongside the error. A caller that ignores the error or checks `len(data)` could write a bogus file.
findings.evidence:
data, err := json.MarshalIndent(r, "", "  ")
		return append(data, '\n'), err

fix.before:
data, err := json.MarshalIndent(r, "", "  ")
		return append(data, '\n'), err

findings.title: Exact float equality on derived grid values
findings.message: Nyquist, Resolution and SampleStep are compared with exact float equality. These values come from floating-point arithmetic over the interval, so the test may fail spuriously if the implementation changes how it computes them (e.g. (end-start)/n vs n/(end-start)).
findings.suggestion: Compare with a small tolerance, e.g. `math.Abs(r.Resolution-2.5) > 1e-12`.

findings.title: Harmonics aliasing mutation is never asserted
findings.message: The test writes to `r.Harmonics[0].Peak` but never checks whether the snapshot's Harmonics slice is aliased. As a result, the Harmonics part of the deep copy is untested.

findings.title: Stale export refusal uses operation ID instead of result ID
findings.message: `cfg.ID` holds the source verification operation ID, not the spectrum result ID. The stale-export check therefore exports an ID that never named a spectrum result. It would be refused for the wrong reason (unknown ID), and it never checks that the retired result itself can no longer be exported.
findings.suggestion: Use `oldID` (the retired spectrum result ID) for the stale-export refusal right after the settings change.
findings.evidence: refuse(t, s, "spectrum.export", VerificationExportParams{ID: cfg.ID, Path: filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "stale.json"), Format: "json"}, "not-ready")

fix.before: refuse(t, s, "spectrum.export", VerificationExportParams{ID: cfg.ID, Path: filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "stale.json"), Format: "json"}, "not-ready")
fix.after: refuse(t, s, "spectrum.export", VerificationExportParams{ID: oldID, Path: filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "stale.json"), Format: "json"}, "not-ready")
